edits.text: The fictional curator asked that future display labels be 35–50 words, with details kept off-label (Trial A). Treat this as trial-specific guidance, not proof that every display has the same constraint. Prior 180–200 word planning assumption is superseded for this exhibit. Keep claims tied to observations: in the indoor trial, flowers opened after sunset and closed the next morning, and 3 of 12 buds opened. No observation establishes a wild pollinator. Routine visitors read the first sentence and large-print species name, while usually skipping the provenance appendix. (Sources: curator trial A; specimen facts; routine visitor observation; failed trials B and C.)

analyses.content: Comparison of label guidance, visitor behavior, and claim accuracy. Source profile records a test-only model and says physical provider sends are unknown; that does not establish zero usage. The current exhibit-label Method says to prefer exhaustive coverage and include every detail before drafting (practice). Its assumption of 180–200 words is explicitly unconfirmed curator planning memory (memory). The specimen facts are bounded observations: the fictional night-blooming cactus opened after sunset and closed the next morning indoors; 3/12 buds opened; no wild pollinator was observed (facts). Routine visitor observations say the first sentence and large-print species name were read while the provenance appendix was usually skipped, with no complaint (ordinary); this suggests prominence matters, but does not prove an optimal length. Trial A reports the fictional curator approved a 42-word draft and asked for 35–50 words on future display labels, details off-label (success). Trial B’s 190-word label went unread because it did not fit; Trial C’s short label failed because it claimed an unsupported wild pollinator (error). Together these support concise, evidence-bound display text for this exhibit, while showing that brevity alone does not ensure accuracy. An alternative explanation for visitor reading patterns could be typography or placement; the sources do not isolate causes. There is no delivered later Work outcome in this history to assess a revised Method. A bounded exploration across the profile, exhibit Method, specimen facts, visitor observation, successful trial, and failed trials found no basis for asserting universal length rules or pollination. Unknown: other exhibit types, display dimensions, and outcomes beyond these supplied trials.
